S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  C482 296 of 2023  Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Harshpal Sekhon, Advocate, for the applicant.
Mr. Atul Kumar Shah, Deputy A.G., with Mrs. Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder, for the State of Uttarakhand.

The instant C482 Application has been preferred by the applicant, by putting a challenge to the cognizance order dated 13th December, 2022, which has been passed by the Court of District and Sessions Judge / Special Judge (SC & ST Act), Nainital, on the basis of the chargesheet, which was submitted on 28th November, 2022, resulting into the registration of Special Sessions Trial No. 15 of 2022, State Vs. Pankaj Kumar, whereby, the present applicant has been summoned to be tried for the offences under Sections 376, 504 and 506 of the IPC and Section 3 (2) (5) (a) of the SC & ST Act.
Apparently, as per the set of allegations levelled in the FIR, the complainant's case is, that she is 25 years of age, and she got in touch with the present applicant through Facebook, as back as in 2018,
and thereafter, their relationship continued, and that fact could be very well established by the Whatsapp Chat, which is admittedly said to have been continued between the complainant and the present applicant, which establishes continuance of their relationship ever since 2018.

entities.text: Court of District and Sessions Judge / Special Judge (SC & ST Act), Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The complainant has admitted the fact in the FIR itself, that she had met the present applicant several times.
She further admits the fact, that she had gone with the present applicant to Ram Nagar and various other places.
She admits the fact, that she had gone to a hotel on the pretext that in future, the applicant would be marrying with her.
She submits, that physical relationship was established by the applicant under an assurance, that the applicant would be marrying with the complainant.

It is not even that, the said relationship eversince 2018, is said to have been repeated when the present applicant is said to have taken the complainant to Garjia Temple, from where, they have Hon'Ble Sharad Kumar Sharma vs The Complainant Has Admitted The Fact In ... on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160137557/
1 gone to a hotel, where they have stayed and there they established physical relationship.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On a simplicitor narration of the case, made in the FIR, it is an admitted fact, that the complainant and the present applicant were known to each other ever since 2018.

It is not in dispute, that the complainant is a major, and she has voluntarily travelled around with the present applicant to several places and had stayed in a hotel, where physical relationships are said to have been established.

Under these set of circumstances, the issue would be as to whether, at all, establishment of physical relationship could be brought within the ambit of offence under Section 376 of the IPC, because the very fact, that she has travelled around to different places and stayed in a hotel itself, shows, that there was a consent and this will amount to be a consensual relationship and will not be a rape within the definition of rape as provided under Section 375 of the IPC.
In that eventuality, let notices be issued to respondent No.2/complainant.
Steps would be taken by the applicant within a period of one week from today.
The respondents may file their counter affidavit within a period of three weeks.

So far as the summoning order dated 13th December, 2022, as issued against the present applicant in Special Sessions Trial No.15 of 2022, State Vs. Pankaj Kumar, pending consideration before the District and Sessions Judge/Special Judge (SC & ST Act), Nainital, would be kept in abeyance, till the next date of listing.

entities.text: District and Sessions Judge/Special Judge (SC & ST Act), Nainital
